regulations.subject: Medical electrical equipment general requirements for basic safety and essential performance

requirements.description: Metal provided with an insulating lining affixed to cord anchorage, except when it is a flexible bushing forming part of the cord guard in 8.11.3.6, and complying with the requirements for one MEANS OF PROTECTION
Cord anchorage prevents cord from being clamped by a screw bearing directly on cord insulation
Screws to be operated when replacing POWER SUPPLY CORD do not serve to secure any components other than parts of cord anchorage
Conductors of POWER SUPPLY CORD arranged to prevent PROTECTIVE EARTH CONDUCTOR against strain as long as phase conductors are in contact with their terminals when cord anchorage fails
Cord anchorage prevents POWER SUPPLY CORD from being pushed into ME EQUIPMENT or MAINS CONNECTOR

Conductors of POWER SUPPLY CORD supplied by a MANUFACTURER disconnected from terminals or from MAINS CONNECTOR and cord subjected 25 times to a pull applied with no jerks, each time for 1 s, on sheath of the value in Table 18
Cord subjected to a torque in Table 18 for 1 min immediately after pull tests
Cord anchorage did not allow cord sheath to be longitudinally displaced by more than 2 mm or conductor ends to move over a distance of more than 1 mm from their connected position
CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES not reduced below limits in 8.9
It was not possible to push the cord into ME EQUIPMENT or MAINS CONNECTOR to an extent the cord or internal parts would be damaged

POWER SUPPLY CORDS other than for STATIONARY ME EQUIPMENT protected against excessive bending at inlet opening of equipment or of MAINS CONNECTOR by means of an insulating cord guard or by means of an appropriately shaped opening
Cord guard complied with test of IEC 60335-1:2001, Clause 25.14
ME EQUIPMENT placed such that axis of cord guard projected at an angle of 45° with cord free from stress, and a mass equal 10 x D² gram attached to the free end of cord
Cord guard of temperature-sensitive material tested at 23 °C ±2 °C, and flat cords bent in the plane of least resistance
Curvature of the cord radius, immediately after mass attached, was not less than 1.5 x D
MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES
PERMANENTLY INSTALLED and ME EQUIPMENT with non-DETACHABLE POWER SUPPLY CORD replaceable by SERVICE PERSONNEL provided with MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES ensuring reliable connection
Terminals alone are not used to keep conductors in position, except when barriers are provided such that CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES cannot be reduced below 8.9 if any conductor breaks away
Terminals of components other than terminal blocks complying with requirements of this Clause and marked according to 7.3.7 used as terminals intended for external conductors
Screws and nuts clamping external conductors do not serve to secure any other component, except they also clamp internal conductors when unlikely to be displaced when fitting the supply conductors
Arrangement of MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES
Terminals provided for connection of external cords or POWER SUPPLY CORDS together with PROTECTIVE EARTH TERMINAL grouped to provide convenient means of connection
PROTECTIVE EARTH CONDUCTOR connections complied with 8.6
Marking of MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES complied with 7.3
MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES not accessible without use of a TOOL
A MEANS OF PROTECTION are not short circuited when one end of a flexible conductor with NOMINAL cross-sectional area is stripped 8 mm and a single free wire is bent in each possible direction
Internal wiring not subjected to stress and CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES not reduced below 8.9 after fastening and loosening a conductor of largest cross-sectional area 10 times

semantic_fragments.content: Cord anchorage requirements (8.11.3.5): After pull and torque tests per Table 18, the cord anchorage shall not allow the cord sheath to be longitudinally displaced by more than 2 mm, nor conductor ends to move over a distance of more than 1 mm from their connected position. CREEPAGE and CLEARANCES shall not be reduced below limits in 8.9, and it shall not be possible to push the cord into ME EQUIPMENT or MAINS CONNECTOR to an extent the cord or internal parts would be damaged.

Cord guard requirements (8.11.3.6): POWER SUPPLY CORDS other than for STATIONARY ME EQUIPMENT shall be protected against excessive bending at the inlet opening of equipment or MAINS CONNECTOR by means of an insulating cord guard or appropriately shaped opening. The cord guard shall comply with IEC 60335-1:2001 Clause 25.14, or alternatively: ME EQUIPMENT placed such that axis of cord guard is at 45° with cord free from stress, a mass equal to 10×D² grams attached to free end of cord, tested at 23°C ±2°C for temperature-sensitive materials, with flat cords bent in the plane of least resistance. Curvature of cord radius immediately after mass attachment shall not be less than 1.5×D.

MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES arrangement requirements (8.11.4.2): (a) Terminals for connection of external cords or POWER SUPPLY CORDS together with PROTECTIVE EARTH TERMINAL shall be grouped to provide convenient means of connection. (b) PROTECTIVE EARTH CONDUCTOR connections shall comply with 8.6. (c) Marking of MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES shall comply with 7.3. (d) MAINS TERMINAL DEVICES shall not be accessible without use of a TOOL. (e) MEANS OF PROTECTION shall not be short-circuited when one end of a flexible conductor with NOMINAL cross-sectional area is stripped 8 mm and a single free wire is bent in each possible direction.
